subject: seahorse
pitch: A lined seahorse holding on to a strand of seagrass with its curled tail. A ridged body in sunny yellow with thin dark lines and a few white freckles, a little crown of spikes on its head, a long tube snout, a delicate fluttering fin on its back, and big, curious eyes.
reasoning:
I'm planning to write a single TypeScript module relying on the SDK primitives I know well—builder functions like joint, chain, sweep, part, extrude, lathe, membrane, ring, and scatter—keeping the scope manageable given I don't have full docs for everything.

For the seahorse itself, I'm designing an upright S-curved body with a forward-facing tube snout, stacked ring segments to form ridged texture with thin dark bands between them, a curled tail using a chain and sweep, a membrane-based back fin, spike crowns on the head, oversized eyes with dark pupils, scattered freckle spheres across the body, and a thin green seagrass strand it's holding.

I'm sketching out the joint hierarchy and spine path coordinates, starting with a hips root joint near the base and a body chain curving upward and slightly forward to position the torso and head.

For the ridged texture along the body, I'm planning to use repeated torus rings swept along the spine path, orienting each ring's geometry so its normal axis aligns with the local tangent direction at each point.

The body itself will be a smooth tube sweep in yellow, with the darker torus ridges stacked on top at intervals. For the tail, I'm working out a curling path that starts at the hips and spirals around a nearby piece of grass, computing the curl points manually so it wraps convincingly around the grass's position.

I'll finish the tail loop with 14 points sweeping outward, then move to the dorsal fin, placing it in the YZ plane along the seahorse's back with thickness extruded along X so it extends backward and upward from the spine.

For the head, I'm planning a sphere shape with a forward-angled snout tube or capsule, then adding eye spheres—a larger white sphere with a smaller dark pupil sphere positioned slightly forward on the head.

For decoration, I'm adding small spike shapes along the crown of the head angled upward and backward, plus tiny white freckle spheres scattered across the body surface using a nearest-point lookup against the trunk sweep. I'm also considering distributing ridge segments along the spine chain path using a repeating placement helper.

For the body itself I'll build it as a sweep along the spine with a roughly constant radius, and I'm thinking through grounding: since the seahorse is depicted clinging to a blade of grass rather than standing, the grass stalk itself should touch the floor at y=0 while the seahorse's body sits higher up, attached to the grass rather than the ground. I'm sketching the grass as a thin tapered blade rising from the floor to about 0.3 units tall, positioned as its own object rather than parented to the seahorse's skeleton.

For the joint hierarchy, I'm figuring out whether to rely on named chains like "spine" to auto-generate joints along a path, or explicitly define joints like hips and head with parent references -- leaning toward minimizing manual joints by letting the spine chain handle most of the skeleton.

Now I'm sketching the actual S-curve of spine points from hips up through chest to the neck and head, then working out the snout's forward-and-downward angle and tip placement, and checking that the tail has enough clearance from the grass blade so it doesn't intersect the body.

I realize the loop would cut through the body, so I shift the grass blade further out to x=0.06 with a tighter loop radius around 0.0145, keeping enough clearance from the body surface while still letting the tail wrap loosely around the grass. I work out the tail's point sequence from hips through a transition into the spiral loop using angle and height interpolation, then move on to planning the head details—eyes, snout, crown spikes, dorsal fin outline, body freckles via nearest-surface placement, and dark ridge rings along the spine using torus shapes slightly larger than the body radius. Finally I start sketching the actual TypeScript module structure, defining color constants, the builder setup, and the hips joint before building out the rest of the creature procedurally.

I decide to trust the SDK's built-in spike helper for the crown spikes rather than fiddling with cone geometry aiming, and work out eye and pupil placement so the pupils sit slightly outside the eye sphere surface for a cartoonish look. I also refine the snout's start and end coordinates relative to the head sphere, and pick freckle positions along the chest/belly that will get projected onto the body surface via the nearest-point method, before finalizing everything into the complete build function.
